newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Shareholders reject Neftochim refinery accounts.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders reject Neftochim refinery accounts.

text.p: A meeting of shareholders in Bulgaria's Neftochim oil refinery voted on Tuesday not to accept the plant's 1996 report and accounts, a day after the government ordered an audit, state radio said.
The state, which holds 75 percent of Neftochim, rejected the two documents on the grounds that they lacked analysis and did not coincide with the figures of the finance ministry.
Bulgaria's government on Monday ordered an audit of the refinery, which posted a loss of 33.4 billion levs ($19.6 million) last year.
The shareholders' meeting replaced most of the members of Neftochim's board of directors. The new board does not include the two present executive directors, Nikola Karagiozov and Atanas Zaekov.
Bulgaria plans to offer up to 75 percent of the indebted refinery for sale to private investors. Several firms including Russia's Rosneft have shown interest in the sale.
The remaining 25 percent of the refinery was sold under Bulgaria's mass privatisation programme.
-- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188 ($ = 1700 Bulgarian Levs)
